statement: A redundant coordinate can be recognized by checking payload/certificate/family-chain irrelevance fields.
Deleting a redundant coordinate and restricting to S without c defines an output witness.
The restricted witness can be renormalized into the selected support normal form.
The output witness has support_size one smaller, hence the lexicographic support measure strictly decreases.
The source and target payload relation is preserved by deleting an unused coordinate.
If the counterexample certificate does not mention c, it transfers to the smaller witness or refutes support-minimality.
Deleting c before canonicalization agrees with canonicalizing then deleting the corresponding redundant coordinate.
Recognized family-chain source form remains recognized when c is outside all family-chain lift fields.
Failure of the redundancy precondition is a named non-application case, not hidden proof success.
For this operation, cases are redundancy success or named non-application/failure.
